title: Supported living review: 'friends' making him withdraw money (synthetic)
setting: A care assessor visits Jamie Coulter, 24, who has a learning disability, at his supported living flat in Bramley Court, Oakhurst, for a review of his support hours.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hiya Jamie, it's Helen. Is it okay if I come in?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Hiya. I've tidied up.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You have, it looks really nice. Is that a new picture on the wall?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's Leeds. Leeds United. My dad got it me.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Brilliant. So, um, do you remember why I'm coming today?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: To talk about my support. My hours.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's right. We're seeing if your support is still right for you. I'll write some notes. If you tell me something that means you might not be safe, I might have to tell other people, so they can help. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Good. So, tell me about your week. What do you do?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Tuesdays and Thursdays I go to the garden centre. I do the plants, the watering. And I get paid.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You get paid? That's great. How do you get paid?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: In the bank. Every two weeks. On a Friday. That's payday.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And how's cooking going? Last time you were learning pasta.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I can do pasta. And beans on toast. Tom helps me on Mondays with the shopping.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Tom's your support worker?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. He's sound.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And what about friends? Who do you see?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: My girlfriend, Kayleigh. And, erm, Dean and Lewis. From the park.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: What do you do with Dean and Lewis?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Hang out. Go to the shop.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Can I ask about money, Jamie? How does money go in your week?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Um. It's... I don't know.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's all right. Take your time. What happens on payday?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Dean and Lewis come. They walk me to the cash machine.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And then what happens?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I have to take out a hundred. £100. And give it them.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Is that every payday?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Every payday. Dean says it's for, um, being mates.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you for telling me, Jamie. What would happen if you didn't give them the money?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: They said they'd hurt me. Dean said he'd hurt me if I didn't.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. That sounds really scary.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, no, forget it. They're my mates. I gave it them. I wanted to.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You don't have to say anything you don't want to, Jamie. You're not in trouble.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't want them to get told off.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I understand. Can I ask you again, though, in your own words? When Dean asks for the money, how do you feel?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Scared. He did say it. He said he'd hurt me if I don't give him it. Last Friday he said it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. You did the right thing telling me. Did they ever actually hurt you?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Just said it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. And after they've had the hundred pounds, have you got enough money left?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Not really. Last month I didn't have money for the electric key. The electric went off.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: For how long?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Two days. It was cold. I had crisps for tea.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'm sorry that happened. Did you tell Tom?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. I said I forgot to top up.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Can I ask about Kayleigh? Does Kayleigh ever take your money, or ask for it?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Kayleigh doesn't take my money. She buys me chips sometimes.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So Kayleigh doesn't take your money?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Never. She's nice.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's good. Now, Jamie, because Dean said he'd hurt you, I need to tell our safeguarding team. Their job is to keep you safe. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Will Dean know it was me?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: We'll be really careful. We'll talk to you before anyone talks to Dean. The police might need to know, but I'll tell you first.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. I don't want police at my flat though.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll write that down, that you don't want police coming to the flat. Now, the next payday is this Friday, the twenty-seventh. What could we do so you're safe?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Dunno.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: What if Tom came with you to the bank on Friday morning? Or your wages stay in the bank and you just use your card in the shop?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Tom could come. Dean won't come if Tom's there.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Good. I'll ring Tom today. And would you like help with a budget, so you know what's for the electric and food?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Like a list.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Like a list, with pictures if you want. Tom can do that with you on Monday.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And your support hours, I think we should ask for more, maybe an extra two hours a week for money. I'll put that in my report.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Will I still go to the garden centre?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Yes, that doesn't change. So, to recap. Today I tell the safeguarding team and ring Tom. Friday, Tom goes with you to the bank. Monday, Tom helps with a budget. And I'll come back on Wednesday the second of December.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Wednesday. Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: If Dean or Lewis come round and you feel scared, ring Tom or the on-call number on your fridge. And if you're in danger, ring 999.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I know. It's on the fridge.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You've done really well today, Jamie.

disclosures.what: Jamie says two men he calls friends, Dean and Lewis, make him take out £100 from the cash machine every payday and give it to them.
Jamie says Dean told him they would hurt him if he did not give them the money; he then says they are his mates and he gave it to them, and then says again that Dean said he would hurt him.
Jamie says that after paying them he had no money for his electric key and the electric was off for two days last month.

controls.must_not_claim: Jamie's girlfriend Kayleigh takes his money.
